passages.text: Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines fought against Israel.
The Philistines were Israel’s enemies.
The men of Israel ran away from the Philistines.
Many men of Israel died on Mount Gilboa.
passages.original: וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים נִלְחָמִ֣ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּנֻ֜סוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיִּפְּל֥וּ חֲלָלִ֖ים בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְבֹּֽעַ׃

passages.text: The Philistines followed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were Israel’s enemies.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul had sons named Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
The Philistines chased Saul and his sons.
The Philistines caught up to them.
The Philistines killed Jonathan.
The Philistines killed Abinadab.
The Philistines killed Malchishua.
Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua were Saul’s sons.
passages.original: וַיַּדְבְּק֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אֶת־ שָׁא֖וּל וְאֶת־ בָּנָ֑יו וַיַּכּ֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים אֶת־ יְהוֹנָתָ֧ן וְאֶת־ אֲבִינָדָ֛ב וְאֶת־ מַלְכִּי־ שׁ֖וּעַ בְּנֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל׃

passages.text: When the battle intensified against Saul, the archers overtook him and wounded him critically.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
The battle became very fierce against Saul.
Archers were men who used bows and arrows.
The archers found Saul.
The archers shot at Saul.
The archers wounded Saul very badly.
passages.original: וַתִּכְבַּ֤ד הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל וַיִּמְצָאֻ֥הוּ הַמּוֹרִ֖ים אֲנָשִׁ֣ים בַּקָּ֑שֶׁת וַיָּ֥חֶל מְאֹ֖ד מֵהַמּוֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and run it through me, or these uncircumcised men will come and run me through and torture me!” But his armor-bearer was terrified and refused to do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
The Philistines were Israel’s enemies.
Saul was badly wounded in battle.
Saul spoke to his armor-bearer.
He said, “Draw your sword.
Kill me with it.
If you do not, these uncircumcised men will come.
They will kill me.
They will torture me.”
The armor-bearer was very afraid.
He refused to kill Saul.
Saul took his own sword.
He fell on it.
He killed himself.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁאוּל֩ לְנֹשֵׂ֨א כֵלָ֜יו שְׁלֹ֥ף חַרְבְּךָ֣׀ וְדָקְרֵ֣נִי בָ֗הּ פֶּן־ יָ֠בוֹאוּ הָעֲרֵלִ֨ים הָאֵ֤לֶּה וּדְקָרֻ֙נִי֙ וְהִתְעַלְּלוּ־ בִ֔י וְלֹ֤א אָבָה֙ נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֔יו כִּ֥י יָרֵ֖א מְאֹ֑ד וַיִּקַּ֤ח שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־ הַחֶ֔רֶב וַיִּפֹּ֖ל עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his own sword and died with him.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul fought in a hard battle against the Philistines.
Saul was wounded very badly by enemy archers.
Saul asked his armor-bearer to kill him with a sword.
The armor-bearer was very afraid and refused.
Saul fell on his own sword and died.
The armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead.
The armor-bearer fell on his own sword.
The armor-bearer died with Saul.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥רְא נֹשֵֽׂא־ כֵלָ֖יו כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת שָׁא֑וּל וַיִּפֹּ֥ל גַּם־ ה֛וּא עַל־ חַרְבּ֖וֹ וַיָּ֥מָת עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men died together that same day.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul died that day.
Saul’s three sons died that day.
Saul’s armor-bearer died that day.
All of Saul’s men died that day.
They all died together.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣מָת שָׁא֡וּל וּשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת בָּנָיו֩ וְנֹשֵׂ֨א כֵלָ֜יו גַּ֧ם כָּל־ אֲנָשָׁ֛יו בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא יַחְדָּֽו׃

passages.text: When the Israelites along the valley and those on the other side of the Jordan saw that the army of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their cities and ran away. So the Philistines came and occupied their cities.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites lived along the valley.
Other Israelites lived on the other side of the Jordan River.
These Israelites saw that the army of Israel had fled.
They also saw that Saul and his sons had died.
The Israelites abandoned their cities.
They ran away.
The Philistines came to those cities.
The Philistines lived in those cities.
passages.original: וַיִּרְא֣וּ אַנְשֵֽׁי־ יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר־ בְּעֵ֨בֶר הָעֵ֜מֶק וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן כִּֽי־ נָ֙סוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְכִי־ מֵ֖תוּ שָׁא֣וּל וּבָנָ֑יו וַיַּעַזְב֤וּ אֶת־ הֶֽעָרִים֙ וַיָּנֻ֔סוּ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיֵּֽשְׁב֖וּ בָּהֶֽן׃ס

passages.text: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were enemies of Israel.
The next day, the Philistines came to the battlefield.
They came to strip the dead bodies.
They found Saul on Mount Gilboa.
They found Saul’s three sons with him.
Saul and his three sons had fallen on Mount Gilboa.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְפַשֵּׁ֖ט אֶת־ הַחֲלָלִ֑ים וַֽיִּמְצְא֤וּ אֶת־ שָׁאוּל֙ וְאֶת־ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת בָּנָ֔יו נֹפְלִ֖ים בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְבֹּֽעַ׃

passages.text: They cut off Saul’s head, stripped off his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temples of their idols and among their people.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines found Saul dead on Mount Gilboa.
They cut off Saul’s head.
They took off his armor.
They sent messengers through the land of the Philistines.
The messengers told the news in the temples of their idols.
The messengers also told the news to the people.
passages.original: וַֽיִּכְרְתוּ֙ אֶת־ רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַיַּפְשִׁ֖יטוּ אֶת־ כֵּלָ֑יו וַיְשַׁלְּח֨וּ בְאֶֽרֶץ־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֜ים סָבִ֗יב לְבַשֵּׂ֛ר בֵּ֥ית עֲצַבֵּיהֶ֖ם וְאֶת־ הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: They put his armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths and hung his body on the wall of Beth-shan.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines took Saul’s armor.
They placed his armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths.
They took Saul’s body.
They hung his body on the wall of Beth-shan.
passages.original: וַיָּשִׂ֙מוּ֙ אֶת־ כֵּלָ֔יו בֵּ֖ית עַשְׁתָּר֑וֹת וְאֶת־ גְּוִיָּתוֹ֙ תָּקְע֔וּ בְּחוֹמַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית שָֽׁן׃

passages.text: When the people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul, all their men of valor set out, journeyed all night, and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-shan. When they arrived at Jabesh, they burned the bodies there.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul.
The Philistines had killed Saul.
The Philistines had hung the bodies of Saul and his sons on the wall of Beth-shan.
All the brave men of Jabesh-gilead got up.
They traveled all night.
They took the body of Saul from the wall of Beth-shan.
They also took the bodies of Saul’s sons from the wall.
They brought the bodies back to Jabesh.
They burned the bodies there.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו יֹשְׁבֵ֖י יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשׂ֥וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים לְשָׁאֽוּל׃ וַיָּק֜וּמוּ כָּל־ אִ֣ישׁ חַיִל֮ וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ כָל־ הַלַּיְלָה֒ וַיִּקְח֞וּ אֶת־ גְּוִיַּ֣ת שָׁא֗וּל וְאֵת֙ גְּוִיֹּ֣ת בָּנָ֔יו מֵחוֹמַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית שָׁ֑ן וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ יָבֵ֔שָׁה וַיִּשְׂרְפ֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Then they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.
passages.sermon: The men of Jabesh-gilead took the bones of Saul and his sons.\r\nThey buried the bones under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh.\r\nThey fasted for seven days.
passages.original: וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת־ עַצְמֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ תַֽחַת־ הָאֶ֖שֶׁל בְּיָבֵ֑שָׁה וַיָּצֻ֖מוּ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃פ
